note: Thresholds for eval/ci_gate.py. Each hit-rate threshold is at or below (hits - 2) / 71 for the committed results file it names, so a two-item loss passes and a three-item loss fails; MRR and nDCG thresholds sit 0.03 below the committed value; the judged thresholds sit under what the named judged run scored on the same ten items (`python -m eval.ci_gate calibrate`). `python -m eval.ci_gate retrieval --dry-run` refuses a threshold above its own calibration value.

judged.subset_note: One or more items from every stratum (single_hop 2, numerical 3, multi_hop 1, list 1, comparative 1, negative 1, temporal 1), chosen for stability on the first index: each was answered identically on the two committed runs of the measured configuration 1.7 hours apart and again under the output contract. On the rebuilt index 8 of the 10 drafts are byte-identical to the first-index contract run and 2 (qa_0047, qa_0057) differ in wording only. qa_0062 (recursion limit on every first-index run of this configuration) and qa_0064 (a correct 'not disclosed' answer the judge scores 0) are left out on purpose; qa_0024, the rebuilt index's one recursion-limit item, is not in the subset.
judged.verify_mode_note: Calibrated on reindex-v3, a strict-mode run on the rebuilt index judged by gemini-3.6-flash, so the judged workflow runs VERIFY_MODE=strict and scores what production serves: the verified answer, or the refusal. A run under another verify mode or another contract version fails regardless of score; recalibrate from a new judged run after changing either. The earlier calibration (facts-v3, first index, no contract) gave faithfulness 1.000, answer_relevancy 0.930, context_recall 0.800, figure_primary 1.000 on the same ten items.
